notes: IMDuel on Ethereum (chain 1): chess played by trades. IMDuelHook constructor arguments in declaration order: manager = $poolManager; engine = the ChessEngineV5 already deployed at 0xc21788f704a8b9456f7391a01d8a3d95be215a27 (the constructor does not check its code, so the hook builds where the engine has none; the address is checked off chain); imd = IMD 0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7; minImd 10 IMD and minImduel 1,000,000 IMDUEL, the smallest pile worth one conversion batch; turnBlocks 3, how many blocks a move takes bids for (about 36 s). No owner, admin, pause, upgrade path or backend signer, so no $owner argument. The token is src/IMDuelToken.sol (IMDuel, IMDUEL, 18 decimals, 1,000,000,000 fixed, minted once to the factory, plain transfers, no owner, mint, burn, tax, pause or blocklist). The factory deploys the token and the hook and opens this pool (IMD pair, LP fee 12500, spacing 60) in one transaction. The first pool opened on the hook is the main duel and must pair IMD (afterInitialize reverts otherwise); its other currency becomes IMDUEL. Every later duel must pair IMD or IMDUEL (NoRoute otherwise; there is no native ETH route) and never gets the opening surcharge. afterInitialize and every other callback accept only the PoolManager. Hook fee: 0.5% of every swap of its pools through beforeSwapReturnDelta / afterSwapReturnDelta, on top of the untouched 1.25% LP fee: 0.4% to the pool's reward pools (war chests), 0.1% protocol slice converted into IMDUEL in the main duel, half kept in the main duel's IMDUEL chest and half burned. In the main duel's first 300 seconds the chest share starts at 25.4% of the swap (0.4% plus 25 points) and falls linearly to 0.4%, all of it to its chests (time only, nothing per wallet; later duels don't have it). A swap must trade its whole order: one its price limit stops early reverts (PartialFill). beforeAddLiquidity only records the pool's in-range liquidity before an add as the block's start liquidity if nothing has sampled that block yet, so liquidity added in a block is never the depth that block's bids are measured against; it never refuses an add and returns no delta. There are no remove callbacks, so the factory's zero-liquidity fee collection runs untouched. A bid's strength is its trade's share of the smallest in-range liquidity the pool had at the start of its three latest sampled blocks. Conversion batches (convert / convertBatch, anyone may call) spend at most 10 minimums, run at most once per block and buy within 0.1% of the most hook-favourable sqrt price the main duel had at the start of its three latest sampled blocks. Play: every swap bids for its team's next move; its owner is the address in hookData (20 bytes packed or 32 bytes ABI-encoded; zero counts as none), else tx.origin, the wallet that signed, so a trade through any router or aggregator earns (a trade relayed for a smart-contract wallet without hookData credits the relayer: known and accepted). The biggest bid owns the move and a new top bid must pay more than 10% over the current one; a move takes bids for 3 blocks after the previous one was played, and the first swap after its window plays it through a gas-capped call to the engine, seeded by the hash of the window's last block (BLOCKHASH, or the EIP-2935 history contract beyond 256 blocks). An engine failure never reverts a swap; an engine starved by the swap's own gas limit reverts it (NotEnoughGas). A move's reward is recorded from its team's chest as owed to its owner and claimed with withdraw(who, c) (anyone may call; it only pays who) or withdrawTo(c, to) (by the owed party); nothing is ever sent inside a trade, so no recipient runs code while a trader's PoolManager is unlocked.
